transcript.text: Here's my chain-of-title concern: While reviewing the patent chain-of-title file, I confirmed that a prior agreement grants a university consortium continuing rights to conduct non-commercial research with the platform. The current draft's broad worldwide exclusivity would conflict with that prior agreement unless we expressly reserve those research rights in the license. I have this documented in my working file but haven't yet circulated a revised license comment. The fix is straightforward — we need to add an express reservation of the university consortium's non-commercial research rights to the draft before it goes to executive approval. Without that carve-out, granting Helixion worldwide exclusive rights would put us in breach of the existing agreement.

In this week's business call with Helixion, I confirmed that their planned deployment model depends on sublicensing the platform only to accredited hospitals, not to unrestricted commercial partners. The current draft permits sublicensing broadly with the licensor's consent, but that's not aligned with what Helixion actually intends to do — and more importantly, leaving the sublicense permission unrestricted creates commercial risk for us. transcript.text: My export-control review found that the platform's controlled technical documentation falls under ECCN 3E001. The license must prohibit transfers to embargoed jurisdictions and require an end-user certificate before any controlled technical documentation is transferred. I have this documented in my working folder, but it hasn't been incorporated into the draft yet. These requirements need to be added before executive approval — without them, we risk export-control violations when Helixion or its sublicensees receive or transfer the controlled technical documentation.
